title: an `extends` clause alone runs no constructor: declaring a subclass of a foreign class is not a foreign call
notes: A heritage clause evaluates the base expression and sets a prototype; it invokes nothing. The byte-identical program one line different — 09-foreign-calls/constructing-a-subclass-of-a-foreign-class-runs-the-base-constructor — is refused, and that is the whole boundary. This shape has already caught one over-correction: a first draft of the rule charged the clause, which broke 17-durable/the-retired-vibelang-flows-specifier-is-not-compiler-owned, a case that declares a subclass of an unresolvable foreign `Action` and never constructs it. That case pins the boundary only as a side effect of pinning something else; this one pins it on purpose.
